children: Monetary policy should remain firmly focused on price stability as inflationary risks persist, says Silvana Tenreyro, chief economist at the IMF. Central banks' policy stances need to be restrictive enough to return inflation to target in a timely manner, preventing a second-round impact. So far, pass-through to core inflation has been contained, but policymakers need to stay on alert, she says. Where commodity price increases and tech-related investment fan pressures, banks need to tighten further. "The appropriate stance will differ across countries, but the objective is the same: to ensure price stability. Central bank independence remains vital in achieving that goal." (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
